claims.text: Ramalinga Raju confessed in a letter to the board that Satyam's profits and cash balances were inflated by billions of rupees
Raju resigned as Chairman on January 8, 2009 and the government appointed a new board
Raju and his brother were arrested on January 10, 2009
Tech Mahindra won the bid to acquire Satyam in a government-managed process in April 2009
Raju and nine others were convicted by a special CBI court in April 2015

outcome.summary: Raju confessed to inflating Satyam's profits by approximately Rs 70 billion (about $1.5 billion). He resigned and was arrested. The Indian government took control and orchestrated a sale to Tech Mahindra, which acquired Satyam in April 2009. The institution survived under new ownership. Raju was convicted in 2015 and sentenced to prison.

timeline.event: Raju sends letter to Satyam board confessing to inflating profits and cash balances by billions of rupees

title: Satyam Computer Services accounting fraud and founder resignation
trigger: Satyam founder Ramalinga Raju confessed to inflating the company's profits and assets by billions of rupees over several years, leading to his resignation and arrest.
